bullets.title: AVGO: Apple extends custom ASIC collaboration through 2031; bulls see $30-40 C28 EPS
bullets.body: Broadcom and Apple filed an 8-K confirming expanded technology collaboration through 2031 with multi-year agreements to develop and supply custom ASIC silicon for multiple Apple product generations. Jefferies bull case models $30-40 C28 EPS with $200-250B ASIC revenue, noting two new customers beyond Google/Anthropic/Meta/OpenAI, potentially including Apple. Stock was +4.5% pre-market.

bullets.title: NVDA: Kyber rack delayed to 2028 on PCB issues; Jensen Huang NDR July 8-9
bullets.body: NVDA's next-gen Kyber NVL144 rack-scale platform for 2027 Rubin Ultra chips is pushed to 2028 due to PCB midplane manufacturability challenges, per SemiAnalysis. The delay opens a competitive window for AMD and Google at the high-performance AI tier. Separately, Morgan Stanley is hosting a non-deal roadshow with CEO Jensen Huang and CFO Colette Kress in LA (Jul 8) and SF (Jul 9).

bullets.title: MU: Citi adds Upside Catalyst Watch; DRAM ASP forecasts raised sharply
bullets.body: Citi adds a 90-day upside catalyst watch on MU, revising 2Q/3Q/4Q26 DRAM ASP growth to +44%/+20%/+13% QoQ vs prior +37%/+13%/+11%, driven by stronger AI CPU demand. MU non-contracted sales represent ~60% of total, and Citi's Aug-Q estimates are above Street consensus. Samsung is expected to confirm ~20% DRAM ASP and ~35-40% NAND ASP increases for 3Q.

bullets.title: AMD: Citi and GS both flag as top semi pick into 2Q26 earnings; GPU share gains expected
bullets.body: Citi and Goldman Sachs both identify AMD as a top Buy into 2Q26 earnings, citing likely GPU share gains in H2 as AI compute remains undersupplied. AWS EC2 GPU instance pricing rose ~20%, signaling tight supply. NVDA's Kyber delay further expands AMD's competitive window at the high-end. Citi's SOX preview notes ~58% of end markets show strong/improving demand.

bullets.title: DDOG: Bernstein downgrades to Market Perform, cuts PT to $226 (-13% implied)
bullets.body: Bernstein analyst Peter Weed cut Datadog to Market Perform from Outperform and lowered the price target to $226 from a higher prior level, implying ~13% downside from $260.36. The FactSet consensus target is $245.82. Stock was -4.6% pre-market on the downgrade.

bullets.title: MSFT: Wolfe cuts PT to $525 on memory-driven capex surge; FY27 FCF turns negative
bullets.body: Wolfe Research cuts MSFT price target to $525 from $570, maintaining Outperform, after raising FY27 capex estimates to $270B (+$40B) driven by memory price increases and a disclosed $11.5B restricted supplier investment. FY27 FCF is now modeled at -$17.4B vs prior +$14.7B, and gross margin is cut to 63.1% vs consensus 66.6%. Azure growth forecast raised to 41% for FY27.

bullets.title: META: Watermelon LLM matches GPT-5.5; cloud resale narrative and excess capacity concerns
bullets.body: META's internal 'Watermelon' LLM reportedly caught up with OpenAI's GPT-5.5 using an order of magnitude more compute than prior model 'Avocado.' A Bloomberg report on META building a cloud business to sell excess GPU capacity sparked the sector-wide semi selloff (SOX -11% in 2 days), though Wolfe and JPM note META-backed capacity represents only ~36-45% of CRWV/NBIS backlog and likely involves older-gen GPUs. META is also reportedly in final talks with Anthropic for $10B Claude access deal.

bullets.title: NFLX: Most crowded short in media/internet ahead of Q2; engagement down 2% YoY
bullets.body: JPM flags NFLX as the most crowded short in media/internet. Engagement growth is anemic at +2% YoY, with second seasons of key shows losing major viewership (One Piece -30%, Beef -70%, The Night Agent -50%+). Global/US MAUs down ~3% YoY per GS, time spent down 7-8% YoY. Investors see $60-80 trading range on 15-20x FY27 EPS of ~$4. Full-year revenue guidance at +11-13% YoY expected to hold; moderate +50bps operating margin raise possible.

bullets.title: TSLA: Quietly launched Miami robotaxi July 3; Piper China Bus Tour in September
bullets.body: TSLA quietly launched a limited robotaxi service in Miami on July 3. Q2 deliveries beat at 480K units (+25% YoY per Lazar). Technical signals show TSLA with a bearish TREND signal from Hedgeye. Piper Sandler is hosting a China Bus Tour in September covering EVs, autonomous tech, and robotics including TSLA.

bullets.title: CMCSA: Sky acquires ITV M&E for up to £1.6B; to become part of NBCUniversal post-separation
bullets.body: Sky agreed to purchase ITV's Media & Entertainment business for up to £1.6B (£1.2B cash upfront + Love Productions £200M + £200M contingent in 2028). Following Comcast's planned separation, Sky and ITV M&E are expected to form part of NBCUniversal. ITV Studios becomes a pure-play content company. Deal expected to close H2 2027. Comcast's Minions & Monsters posted a franchise-low $36.4M domestic opening.

bullets.title: FWONK: Morgan Stanley reiterates Top Pick at $120; F1 underpenetrated in US/China
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reiterates Formula One (FWONK) as Top Pick with $120 PT ($135 bull case) and Overweight. FY27 FCF/share estimated at ~$4.27, trading at ~22x vs historical 25-30x. Key upside drivers: Germany media rights renewal in 2027 (Amazon/Apple/Netflix/DAZN bidders), untapped AI/LLM sponsorships, licensing doubling/quadrupling potential, and Vegas GP pacing ahead of prior year.

bullets.title: ORCL: Piper sees $2.2B OCI revenue upside in FY27 from ~2,400 MW of new capacity
bullets.body: Piper Sandler estimates ORCL could generate ~$2.2B of incremental OCI cloud revenue in FY27 not in current consensus estimates as ~2,400 MW of data center capacity comes online. New CFO viewed as potentially more prudent on guidance; apps business expectations are reasonable for FY27. Revenue growth seen accelerating.

bullets.title: AFRM: Piper bullish on BNPL 2.0 shift; Affirm Edge adds optionality not in estimates
bullets.body: Piper Sandler views AFRM as one of the clearest beneficiaries of BNPL's evolution from transaction financing to everyday money management. Consumers are shifting toward debit-discipline spending models and AFRM's Affirm Edge product adds upside optionality not currently embedded in consensus estimates.

bullets.title: UBER: Pausing European food delivery expansion amid Delivery Hero pursuit
bullets.body: Uber is pulling back on planned food delivery expansion into 5 of 7 targeted European countries as it pursues the Delivery Hero acquisition. JPM noted the Uber-Waymo Phoenix robotaxi pilot reached a natural end; Austin and Atlanta partnerships continue to expand.

bullets.title: HUBS: Oppenheimer flags limited GTM disruption; AI pipeline expectations higher
bullets.body: Oppenheimer channel checks show HubSpot partners see limited lead-gen disruption from the recent sales motion reset, with demand trends mirroring Q1 patterns. Pipeline expectations are rising on growing AI adoption. Some customer hesitation on multi-year commitments; agencies positive on updated outcome-based pricing. Revenue Hub re-skinning is a potential expansion area but demand not expected until year-end.

bullets.title: FOXA: Wolfe upgrades to Outperform at $71; ROKU deal selloff overdone
bullets.body: Wolfe upgrades FOXA to Outperform with a $71 price target, calling the ~20% post-deal selloff an overreaction to the $22B ROKU acquisition. Pro forma FOXA trades at 11.8x fully synergized NTM UFCF with $400M in cost synergies and untapped revenue upside as linear TV shifts to multi-channel CTV compounder with 45% of engagement from streaming.

bullets.title: LITE/CIEN/FN/COHR: JPM positive on LITE/APH/FLEX; Wolfe shows 55-65% upside on data center basket
bullets.body: JPM rates LITE as highest-conviction long with constructive upside sentiment; COHR and FN shifted negative ahead of prints on GLW difficult setup and EML supply concerns. Wolfe's data center basket shows LITE at 64.8% PT upside ($1,200), CIEN at 56.2% ($660), and FN at 55.1% ($775), all Outperform. AI hardware/networking stocks were down ~10-20% last week on overbuild fears but JPM sees strong demand and tight supply with 2027+ backlog.

bullets.title: RDDT: +17% last week on DAU momentum and renewed AI licensing deals
bullets.body: RDDT was the top Internet performer last week at +17%. JPM attributes the move to DAU growth headroom and renewed AI licensing framework deals with Google and OpenAI. Similarweb data shows RDDT gaining AI-driven traffic, and JPM notes renewed engagement momentum.

bullets.title: BE: Bloom Energy secures $25B Brookfield financing (5x expansion) for AI data centers
bullets.body: Bloom Energy secured a $25B financing commitment from Brookfield's dedicated $100B AI Infrastructure Fund, a 5x expansion from the prior $5B facility, to accelerate fuel cell deployment for AI data centers. JPMorgan initiated EROC at Overweight ($24 PT) and INIO at Overweight ($44 PT) on data center power demand; GEV was selected to supply 14 BWRX-300 SMR units (4.2GW) for a UK nuclear fleet.

bullets.title: PLTR: +14.5% last week; MU/COHR/SNDK among biggest S&P losers (-12-17%)
bullets.body: S&P 500 weekly movers: PLTR gained +14.5% w/w (down 27.3% YTD). On the downside, SNDK fell 16.5% w/w (still +635% YTD), MU lost 13.8% w/w (+242% YTD), COHR dropped 12.4% w/w, and CIEN fell 11.9% w/w. The S&P 500 was +1.8% w/w.
